name: Eureka Tower
bio_draft: Eureka Skydeck on level 88 with panoramic views over the city.

facts.claim: Melbourne Skydeck is the observation deck at the top of Eureka Tower, billed as the highest in the southern hemisphere
The Edge is a glass cube that extends 3 metres out from the side of the building
Bar 88 serves food and drinks with the views

access_note: Name on the site is Melbourne Skydeck; eurekaskydeck.com.au redirects to it. Adult online $33-43 by time; The Edge is an extra.

name: Old Melbourne Gaol
bio_draft: 1850s gaol open to visitors with daytime tours and night tours.

facts.claim: Victoria's oldest prison, run as a museum with day tours and night tours (Hangman's, Ghosts)
Ned Kelly's Last Stand guided tour runs on weekends for $7 on top of general admission
Cells are devoted to the women and children of the gaol

name: Melbourne Zoo
bio_draft: Australia's oldest zoo, opened in 1861, in Royal Park.

facts.claim: Zoos Victoria's Melbourne Zoo in Royal Park, open daily
Home to critically endangered western lowland gorillas
Has play spaces and animal talks

access_note: Adult 'from $58'; kids 0-3 free, children free on weekends and holidays.

name: Werribee Open Range Zoo
bio_draft: open-range zoo within Werribee Park with African and Asian animals.

facts.claim: Zoos Victoria's wildlife safari in Melbourne's west with a free safari bus
Nine Asian elephants roam the Elephant Trail
Deluxe Safari Adventure is offered as an upgrade

name: Heide Museum of Modern Art
bio_draft: modern art museum with a sculpture garden in Bulleen.

facts.claim: Public art museum and sculpture park on the Birrarung/Yarra River in Bulleen
The gardens and sculpture park are free to enter
Heide Kitchen cafe on site

access_note: Gallery adult $27; gardens and sculpture park free. Closed Mondays except public holidays; North East Link works nearby.

name: Immigration Museum
bio_draft: immigration history museum in the restored Old Customs House on Flinders Street.

facts.claim: Museums Victoria museum at 400 Flinders Street, in the Old Customs House
Explores migration to Victoria through galleries including the Customs Gallery

access_note: Adult $15 per search snippet of the official page; seniors price conflicting.
unresolved: official page BLOCKED: https://museumsvictoria.com.au/immigrationmuseum/ - confirm $15 and ticketUrl in a browser

name: Australian Centre for the Moving Image
bio_draft: film, television, games and new media museum with cinemas, in Federation Square.

facts.claim: ACMI is Australia's national museum of screen culture, at Federation Square opposite Flinders Street Station
Its ongoing Story of the Moving Image exhibition on film, TV, videogames and digital culture is free
Temporary exhibitions and cinema screenings are ticketed separately

name: Arts Centre Melbourne
bio_draft: concert hall, theatres and the Arts Centre spire; tours and performances on most days.

facts.claim: Performing arts precinct on St Kilda Road with theatres, Hamer Hall and the landmark spire
Designed by Roy Grounds; the gallery opened 1968 and the theatres and concert hall followed
Guided tours are listed as not currently available; a Collection Store tour is about $43 adult

access_note: Entering the buildings and foyers is understood free; shows and tours are ticketed (not verified on official page). Guided tours reported unavailable.
unresolved: Official site gave no readable text (script wall); free-entry claim and title unconfirmed. Check in a real browser.

name: St Patrick's Cathedral
bio_draft: Gothic Revival cathedral begun in the 1850s, open to visitors on weekdays.

facts.claim: Gothic Revival cathedral designed by William Wardell, built 1858 to 1939 in bluestone
Seat of the Catholic Archbishop of Melbourne, consecrated 1897, on Gisborne Street in East Melbourne
On the Victorian Heritage Register

access_note: Free entry unverified on official page; visiting hours not recorded.
unresolved: free entry not confirmed on official page

name: St Paul's Cathedral
bio_draft: Gothic revival cathedral on Flinders Street, open daily to visitors.

facts.claim: Anglican cathedral of Melbourne at Flinders Street opposite Federation Square
Described as Victoria's most visited sacred place, with over 400,000 visitors a year
Open daily with free admission

name: Fitzroy Gardens
bio_draft: historic gardens with an avenue of English elms and a conservatory, next to Cooks' Cottage.

facts.claim: Heritage-listed gardens set aside as a reserve in 1848 in East Melbourne, about 26 hectares
Lawns and paths lined with mature elm trees in Victorian-era design
Contains the Conservatory, Cooks' Cottage and a visitor centre

name: Cooks' Cottage
bio_draft: the parents' cottage of Captain James Cook, moved to Fitzroy Gardens, open daily with entry fee.

facts.claim: Cottage built in 1755 in Yorkshire by the parents of Captain James Cook
Moved to Melbourne in 1934 by Sir Russell Grimwade and rebuilt in Fitzroy Gardens
Surrounded by an English cottage garden; tickets sold at the Fitzroy Gardens Visitor Centre

unresolved: adult price $7.70 comes from a search snippet of the council's event page (older council page said $7.20); not confirmed in fetched text

name: Parliament House of Victoria
bio_draft: Victorian parliament house with public tours on weekdays and weekends.

facts.claim: Parliament House opened in 1856, with the two chambers built first
It offers a free public tour and a free architecture tour

access_note: Tours are not available when Parliament is sitting or on some days; no hours recorded

name: Carlton Gardens
bio_draft: gardens around the Royal Exhibition Building, with lawns and fountains.

facts.claim: 26-hectare Victorian-era gardens around the Royal Exhibition Building and Melbourne Museum
Part of the UNESCO-listed Royal Exhibition Building and Carlton Gardens World Heritage site

name: Melbourne Park
bio_draft: Melbourne Park tennis centre and arenas beside the Yarra, home of the Australian Open.

facts.claim: Home of the Australian Open tennis since 1988, beside Jolimont Yard
Rod Laver Arena seats about 15,000 and hosts concerts as well as tennis

access_note: Venues are ticketed per event; precinct grounds access not confirmed on page
unresolved: whether precinct is free to walk through not confirmed; events ticketed separately

name: Albert Park and Lake
bio_draft: lakeside parkland south of the city, with the Grand Prix circuit around it.

facts.claim: 225-hectare urban park around an artificial lake, 3 km south of the CBD
A 4.7 km walking track circles the lake, with views back to the city skyline
Hosts the Albert Park Circuit of the Australian Grand Prix since 1996

name: Block Arcade
bio_draft: 1892 mosaic-floored shopping arcade linking Collins and Elizabeth Streets.

facts.claim: Built 1891-93 to designs by Twentyman & Askew, listed on the Victorian Heritage Register
Mosaic tiled floors, glass canopy and an octagonal rotunda link Collins and Elizabeth Streets
Home to The Tea Rooms 1892, the original Hopetoun Tea Rooms

name: Royal Arcade
bio_draft: 1870 Bourke Street arcade with a shop front and mosaic floor.

facts.claim: Opened in 1870, the oldest surviving arcade in Australia, designed by Charles Webb
Gog and Magog figures strike the bells of Gaunt's clock each hour
Links Bourke Street Mall, Little Collins Street and Elizabeth Street

name: St Kilda Pier
bio_draft: the St Kilda pier and breakwater, with the kiosk at its end and little penguins at dusk.

facts.claim: A 300 metre elevated pier joined to a 750 metre stone breakwater in Port Phillip Bay.
The historic St Kilda Pavilion kiosk stands at the end of the pier.
A colony of about 1200 little penguins breeds among the breakwater rocks, with public viewing.

unresolved: Entry freeness inferred (open public pier); no official fee page loaded

name: Rippon Lea Estate
bio_draft: heritage mansion and gardens in Elsternwick.

facts.claim: A heritage-listed mansion and 14 acres of gardens in Elsternwick, cared for by the National Trust.
Built for businessman Sir Frederick Sargood, who bought the land in 1868; grounds include a lake, iron-framed fernery, ballroom and stables.
Mansion entry is by guided tour only, bought as an add-on to garden admission.

name: Werribee Park
bio_draft: Werribee Mansion and gardens, a 19th-century estate open to visitors.

facts.claim: An estate built on the wealth of an Australian pastoral empire, with the heritage-listed Werribee Mansion.
Formal gardens include an ornamental lake and grotto; the Victoria State Rose Garden has about 5000 roses.
Entry to the gardens and rose garden is free; the mansion costs $12.50 adult.

access_note: Parks Victoria page shows 'This area has reported issues' banners; check current status

name: Melbourne Aquarium
bio_draft: aquarium on Flinders Street with over 10,000 aquatic creatures in several zones.

facts.claim: Aquarium on the Yarra beside the Flinders Street Viaduct, with over 10,000 animals of 550+ species.
Exhibits include king and gentoo penguins, sharks, jellyfish and a saltwater crocodile.
Opened 17 January 2000 as a Southern Ocean and Antarctic aquarium.

name: Crown Entertainment Complex
bio_draft: casino and resort precinct on the Yarra at Southbank.

facts.claim: Integrated resort of casino, hotels, restaurants and shops on the south bank of the Yarra in Southbank.
Opened at its permanent site on 8 May 1997.
Under-18s may enter the entertainment and shopping areas but not the gaming floor.

unresolved: No entry fee stated on the site; free inferred. Spot may fail the qualifies test (venue is a casino/shops).

name: Ian Potter Centre
bio_draft: Australian art galleries of the National Gallery of Victoria at Federation Square.

facts.claim: The home of Australian art at Federation Square, presenting Indigenous and non-Indigenous historical and contemporary art and design.
Part of the National Gallery of Victoria; entry is free, with fees only for special exhibitions.
